headline: October 30 is shaping up as the heaviest layoff week of October with 8,520 workers affected
summary: The week of October 30 is projected to see 8,520 workers affected by layoffs, a significant jump from the prior week. This makes it the heaviest layoff week of October, though November 13 currently holds the overall peak for scheduled job losses.
details: The week of October 30 is set to be the heaviest layoff week of October, with 8,520 workers scheduled for layoffs. This figure is based on WARN notices filed with state labor agencies, indicating employers' announced intentions for mass job cuts.

WARN notices serve as a forward-looking indicator of potential job losses, though the numbers can change as plans are revised or dates shift. They provide the closest available 'layoff calendar' for the United States.

The weeks of October 30 and November 13 stand out significantly, together accounting for 17,264 scheduled layoffs. This represents more than a quarter of all reported workers within the current 90-day window.

There's a stark contrast with the preceding week of October 23, which had only 1,393 workers scheduled for layoffs. This type of sharp increase is typical, as many WARN notices are effective at month-ends or before holiday periods.

While October 30 is the heaviest week of its month, November 13 currently holds the distinction as the heaviest overall week with 8,744 scheduled workers. November as a whole appears heavy, with over 21,600 scheduled layoffs across the weeks of November 13, 20, and 27.

Geographically, Washington leads all states with 16,938 reported workers in the 90-day window, followed by California (14,224), Illinois (4,626), Texas (3,652), and Ohio (3,180). These figures span 51 jurisdictions, with 48 having imported records.

These totals are dynamic, constantly shifting as new notices are filed and older ones move out of the 90-day window. The October 30 total could still increase as more employers file notices with effective dates in that week, potentially surpassing the November 13 peak.

headline: WhatsApp starts testing scheduled messages on iPhone after years of user requests
summary: After years of anticipation, WhatsApp is finally making one of its most-requested messaging features available to select iPhone beta testers.
details: WhatsApp has begun testing its long-awaited scheduled messages feature with a select group of iPhone beta testers. This functionality allows users to compose messages and set a specific date and time for them to be sent automatically.

The feature addresses a significant user demand, offering convenience for reminders, birthday wishes, or coordinating communications across different time zones. It aims to enhance the planning capabilities within the popular messaging app.

While currently limited to a beta rollout on iOS, the move signals an eventual wider release to all users. Details regarding availability for Android users or a definitive public launch date have not yet been disclosed.
